y-m-09-01.s.s1.prompt: Information dey show one piece at a time. Each time, choose your idea about which angle bigger.

y-m-09-01.s.s1.hint.1: When putting right-angle paper on angle, use your hand act out how paper side and other angle side lie.

y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Di sides short no mean say e bend more. Same thing for long sides.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.0.o.c: Both angles na the same because each get two sides.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Every angle get two sides. Dis fact alone no let you compare sizes.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.0.o.d: We no fit decide yet. We no know how wide both angles open.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Dis idea treat side length and how wide angle open as different information.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.info: When I match corner of right-angle paper with vertex of Angle ㄱ and put one side on top, other side of Angle ㄱ fit exactly with other side of paper. I do same for Angle ㄴ, and e fit exactly too.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.ask: How you fit compare both angles with dis new information?
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.after: Even though side lengths different, 3 cm and 6 cm, both angles get the same size (right angle). First idea "longer sides mean bigger angle" no fit dis evidence.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Angle ㄴ bigger. Im sides na 6 cm, so e cover more paper.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.r.a: You suppose compare direction wey sides dey, no be area e cover for paper. Read di observation "e fit exactly" again.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.o.b: Angle ㄱ bigger. Short sides fit paper better.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Wetin dem observe no be "fit better", na "both fit exactly."
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.o.c: Both angles get same size. Both na right angles.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Dis thinking compare based on result of holding dem against same standard (right-angle paper).
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.o.d: We no fit decide yet. We gatz make sides longer and check again.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Even if you make sides longer, direction wey dem lie no change. Think whether observation wey you already get enough.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.info: I draw Angle ㄷ and Angle ㄹ too. Both angles get sides of 2 cm. When I place right-angle paper, other side of Angle ㄷ dey inside paper side, and other side of Angle ㄹ dey outside paper side.

y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.after: Di two angles with same side length 2 cm (ㄷ and ㄹ) too get different sizes. Some angles same even though lengths different, and some different even though lengths same, so side length no decide angle size.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.o.a: Angle ㄷ. E dey inside paper sides, so e open wider.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Check by holding paper there whether "inside" mean e open more or less.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.o.b: Angle ㄹ. E open outside paper sides.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Dis idea compare angle wey open outside side of right-angle paper with right angle.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.o.c: We no fit know. Di three angles no all get same side length.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Even if sides no be same length, you fit compare using result of putting dem against right-angle paper.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.o.d: Angle ㄱ. Im side longest at 3 cm.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.st.2.r.d: New information for dis step no be side length, na result of holding dem against paper.
y-m-09-01.s.s1.reflect: At first, holding off judgment fit because we only know side lengths. When we hold dem against same standard, right-angle paper, some angles same even though side lengths different (ㄱ and ㄴ), and some different even though side lengths same (ㄷ and ㄹ). Talk which information at which step change your thinking.
y-m-09-01.s.s2.prompt: Clock hour hand and minute hand get different lengths. Among times when minute hand point to 12, find two different times when both hands make right angle. (Write which o'clock, from 1 o'clock to 12 o'clock.)

y-m-09-01.s.s2.hint.1: Look what shape e make for cases wey no be right angle too (when hands make straight line or overlap).

y-m-09-01.s.s2.fail.c2: At dis time, both hands no make right angle. Put right-angle paper on clock shape.
y-m-09-01.s.s2.explain: At 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock, both hands make right angle. At 6 o'clock both hands make straight line, and at 12 o'clock dem overlap, so those no be right angles. Both hands different lengths, but angle size depend on how wide both hands open.
y-m-09-01.s.s3.prompt: Wetin you wan tell Mina? Write why angle size no fit decide from side length, using examples you find above (Angle ㄱ and ㄴ, or two clock hands).
y-m-09-01.s.s3.hint.0: Remember di time above when both angles side lengths different but result of placing right-angle paper be same.
y-m-09-01.s.s3.hint.1: First tell Mina in one sentence "wetin I check", then write di reason.
y-m-09-01.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Mina, even if di sides ...

y-m-09-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You write with your own words wetin decide angle size (how wide both sides open)?
y-m-09-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You write in tone wey understand why Mina think so?
y-m-09-01.s.s3.model.0: Even if sides long, angle size remain the same. You gatz look how wide both sides open. If you place right-angle paper, angle with 3 cm sides and angle with 6 cm sides both fit exactly, so dem get same size.
y-m-09-01.s.s3.model.1: Angle size no get anything to do with side length. Clock hour hand and minute hand get different lengths, but for 3 o'clock dem make right angle. Angle with 3 cm sides and angle with 6 cm sides too fit right-angle paper the same way.
y-m-09-01.s.s3.model.2: Angle ㄱ get sides of 3 cm and Angle ㄴ get sides of 6 cm, so lengths different, but both fit right-angle paper exactly, so both na right angles. So you no fit decide angle size by side length.
y-m-09-01.s.s3.model.3: Long hand and short hand of clock different lengths, but for 3 o'clock dem make right angle. Angle size depend on how wide e open.

y-m-09-03.title: E really be 2 km from house reach library?
y-m-09-03.topic: Length units (km, m) and distance wey you measure along road
y-m-09-03.goal: Realize say even if na same calculation, whether e correct or wrong depend on which road length you dey talk about, and distinguish wetin you fit settle from wetin you no fit settle when new information come.
y-m-09-03.material: Hajun talk, "From house to school na 1 km 200 m, and from school to library na 800 m. So from house to library na 2 km!" You never see map yet. All lengths mean "distance wey you walk along road." (1 km na 1000 m. Dem read km as kilometer and m as meter.)
y-m-09-03.thinking.0: Finding conditions wey make claim hold
y-m-09-03.thinking.1: Separating wetin you fit settle and wetin you no fit settle when new information arrive
y-m-09-03.prereq.0: Knowing 1 km na 1000 m and working with lengths written in km and m (Grade 3 level)
y-m-09-03.prereq.1: Understanding meaning of road wey connect places for map
y-m-09-03.s.s1.prompt: Which case make Hajun statement surely correct?
y-m-09-03.s.s1.hint.0: Write both lengths Hajun talk, each one from where to where, in order "house, school, library."
y-m-09-03.s.s1.hint.1: Draw two or three roads wey "from house reach library" fit mean, and check whether each road pass through both sections.
y-m-09-03.s.s1.o.a: Di case where you mean length of one new road wey go straight from house reach library
y-m-09-03.s.s1.r.a: You no fit know length of new road from dis information. Look again which road dem mean.
y-m-09-03.s.s1.o.b: Di case where you mean length when library dey on same road between house and school
y-m-09-03.s.s1.r.b: If library dey closer to house than school, distance from house to library suppose shorter than from house to school. Dis value dey change with location.
y-m-09-03.s.s1.o.c: Di case where you mean length of road from house, pass through school, reach library
y-m-09-03.s.s1.r.c: Dis thinking check whether you mean one road made from both connected sections.
y-m-09-03.s.s1.o.d: Di case where you mean shortest road from house reach library
y-m-09-03.s.s1.r.d: Dem no settle say shortest road na the one wey pass through school. We no know other roads yet.
y-m-09-03.s.s1.explain: Road wey you walk from house through school reach library na road wey join both sections, so e be 1 km 200 m plus 800 m, wey equal 2000 m, or 2 km. If you mean other roads or other positions, you no fit talk say dis value correct.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.prompt: Teacher tell us, "Dem build new road wey connect house and library directly. We still no know how long di road be. Now only two roads dey from house reach library: 'road through school' and 'new road'." Wetin you fit talk about "length of shortest road to walk from house reach library"?
y-m-09-03.s.s2.hint.0: Imagine case where new road very short and case where e very long, and write which road be shortest for each.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.hint.1: Find whether one fact dey wey no change no matter how long new road be.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.o.a: Na exactly 2 km. Road through school na 2 km, so e remain same.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.r.a: Maybe you miss say new road fit shorter than 2 km.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.o.b: E no pass 2 km. For exact value, you need know new road length.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.r.b: Dis thinking use fact say since one road wey we know already dey, shortest road no fit longer than am.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.o.c: E shorter than 2 km. Na because new road go straight.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.r.c: Road wey go straight no always short. We no know new road length yet.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.o.d: We no fit tell. If we no know new road length, nothing we fit talk.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.r.d: Even if one thing no dey known, think whether you fit talk something from road wey you already know.
y-m-09-03.s.s2.explain: Road through school na 2 km, so shortest road na 2 km or less. If new road shorter than 2 km, na new road be shortest; if e longer than 2 km, road through school still na shortest, 2 km. You fit only talk exact value if you know new road length.
y-m-09-03.s.s3.prompt: Dem find out say new road na 1 km 500 m. Write which road shortest from house reach library, and how many m e shorter pass road through school.
y-m-09-03.s.s3.hint.0: Write both road lengths side by side with same unit.
y-m-09-03.s.s3.hint.1: After you decide which one longer, find how much dem different.
y-m-09-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You decide which road shortest by comparing lengths?
y-m-09-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You compare km and m after matching dem to one unit?
y-m-09-03.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You fit explain again how you know road through school na 2 km?
y-m-09-03.s.s3.model.0: Shortest road na new road (1 km 500 m). Road through school na 2 km or 2000 m, and new road na 1500 m, so new road 500 m shorter.
y-m-09-03.s.s3.model.1: Taking new road na shortest. Road through school na 1 km 200 m joined with 800 m, wey make 2 km, and new road na 1 km 500 m, so difference between roads na 500 m.

y-m-09-04.title: Guessing weight of one apple with balance scale
y-m-09-04.topic: Weight (g) and finding range by comparing with balance scale
y-m-09-04.goal: Even if you no fit know exact value, state a range for weight from comparison results, make range smaller with new observations, and think about limit of whether tools wey you get now fit make am smaller again.
y-m-09-04.material:
Put apple for one side of balance scale and weights for other side to compare. Heavier side go down, and if weights equal, scale level. Several weights each of 50 g, 100 g, 200 g, and 500 g dey. Assume several apples dey wey all weigh exactly the same, and weight of 1 apple na natural number in g.
Observation 1: 1 apple vs two 200 g weights → apple side go down.
Observation 2: 1 apple vs one 500 g weight → weight side go down.
y-m-09-04.thinking.0: Reasoning out range from comparison results
y-m-09-04.thinking.1: Making several values wey fit all conditions
y-m-09-04.thinking.2: Thinking about tool limits and designing next experiment
y-m-09-04.prereq.0: Knowing meaning of g and kg, and say 1 kg na 1000 g (Grade 3 level)
y-m-09-04.prereq.1: Knowing say heavier side go down on balance scale
y-m-09-04.prereq.2: Comparing number sizes and saying dem as "greater than, less than"
y-m-09-04.s.s1.prompt: From only Observation 1 and Observation 2, wetin you fit talk about weight of 1 apple?
y-m-09-04.s.s1.hint.0: For each observation, mark which side go down and write one line saying dat side heavier.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.hint.1: Put both lines side by side and mark section wey apple weight fit dey on number line.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.o.a: E heavier than 400 g and lighter than 500 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.r.a: Dis idea rewrite di side wey go down and di side wey go up as number comparisons.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.o.b: E exactly 500 g, because dem compare am with 500 g weight.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.r.b: Dis thinking see weight of weight wey dem use to compare as apple weight. Look again which side go down.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.o.c: E exactly 450 g. E exactly halfway between 400 g and 500 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.r.c: Dis idea decide say e exactly halfway between both values. No evidence anywhere say e halfway.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.o.d: We no fit know anything. Dem gatz balance am to know weight.
y-m-09-04.s.s1.r.d: Even if e no balance, you still get information "heavier" or "lighter."
y-m-09-04.s.s1.explain: For Observation 1 apple side go down, so apple heavier than 400 g; for Observation 2 weight side go down, so e lighter than 500 g. We no fit settle exact value yet, and we fit only talk say e dey between 401 g and 499 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.prompt: Observation 3 don add. Observation 3: 1 apple vs (two 200 g weights and one 50 g weight) → apple side go up. Write 3 different weights (g) of 1 apple wey fit all three observations.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.hint.0: Write each observation as "apple weight heavier/lighter than ○○ g", then choose one number wey fit all three lines.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.hint.1: Put di number wey you choose inside all three lines one by one, and if any observation disagree, change am.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.ok.c1: Weight na natural number in g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg write weight as natural number in g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.ok.c2: E agree with Observation 1: e heavier than 400 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.fail.c2: E no agree with Observation 1. Apple side go down, so e must heavier than 400 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.ok.c3: E agree with Observation 2: e lighter than 500 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.fail.c3: E no agree with Observation 2. Weight side go down, so e must lighter than 500 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.ok.c4: E agree with Observation 3: e lighter than 450 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.fail.c4: E no agree with Observation 3. Apple side go up, so e must lighter than 450 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s2.explain: Weights wey fit all three observations na natural numbers from 401 g to 449 g. More observations make range smaller, but e never settle on one value.
y-m-09-04.s.s3.prompt: Using only weights we get now (50 g, 100 g, 200 g, 500 g), we fit make apple weight range 401 to 449 g any smaller? If yes, write how to compare with numbers; if no, write reason.
y-m-09-04.s.s3.hint.0: Write all weights wey you fit compare with when you put 1 apple on, and check whether those weights dey inside range 401 to 449 g.
y-m-09-04.s.s3.hint.1: Write how weights you fit compare with change when you change number of things wey you put on scale pan.
y-m-09-04.s.s3.placeholder: e.g., We fit / no fit make range smaller. Because ...
y-m-09-04.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You think about which weight intervals you fit compare with when you put only 1 apple on?
y-m-09-04.s.s3.selfAssess.1: When you put several apples, you write comparison value against weight for other side as number (e.g. 850 g) and change am to weight of one apple?
y-m-09-04.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You check with numbers how range change using your method?
y-m-09-04.s.s3.model.0: If you put 2 apples on at once, you fit make range smaller. Two apples weigh between 802 g and 898 g, and if you put 850 g (one each of 500 g, 200 g, 100 g, and 50 g weights) on other side, you fit tell whether both heavier or lighter than 850 g, so you learn whether one heavier or lighter than 425 g.

y-m-09-06.title: If we sort by "fun books", result go be same no matter who sort?
y-m-09-06.goal: Learn conditions for sorting rule wey give same result no matter who sort, check how sorting result dey change when you change number for rule, and rewrite vague rule as clear one.
y-m-09-06.material:
You wan sort 10 class library books into two shelf rows. Each book get sorting label for spine, and page number written on each book.
Book 1: storybook, 64 pages / Book 2: science, 120 pages / Book 3: social studies, 48 pages / Book 4: storybook, 150 pages / Book 5: science, 200 pages / Book 6: old tales, 36 pages / Book 7: science, 88 pages / Book 8: storybook, 96 pages / Book 9: diary, 24 pages / Book 10: math, 130 pages.
You wan use rule wey go give same result even if three students in charge of arranging dem change.
y-m-09-06.thinking.1: Checking say result dey change when rule change

y-m-09-06.prereq.1: Reading book information like spine label and number of pages
y-m-09-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose all rules wey split 10 books into same two shelves no matter who sort.
y-m-09-06.s.s1.hint.0: Imagine three different people using each rule and look for book wey dem fit put on different shelves.
y-m-09-06.s.s1.hint.1: For each rule, write which part of book you look at to sort (spine, pages, feeling, etc.) and mark which ones you fit check with your eyes.

y-m-09-06.s.s1.r.a: Fun different for each person, so same book fit go on different shelves.

y-m-09-06.s.s1.r.c: How easy book be to read fit feel different for each person.

y-m-09-06.s.s1.r.d: Dis ting sort am by looking di letters wey dey di spine.
y-m-09-06.s.s1.o.e: Books wey get fine cover / books wey no fine
y-m-09-06.s.s1.r.e: Wetin fine fit different for each person.

y-m-09-06.s.s2.prompt: You choose to sort by number of pages. y-m-09-08.title: How much should one picture represent to make picture graph easier to read?
y-m-09-08.topic: Choosing di value one picture represent for picture graph
y-m-09-08.goal: Think about conditions to show di data values exactly with big and small pictures. Confirm say several picture values fit di conditions, then choose di one wey easier to read and give reason.
y-m-09-08.material:
You wan show how much potato four farm fields harvest for picture graph. Field 가 get 120 kg, field 나 get 85 kg, field 다 get 45 kg, and field 라 get 30 kg. You go use 2 kinds of pictures: one big picture represent B kg and one small picture represent s kg. (kg dey read as kilogram.) Di rules be these.
(1) One big picture suppose be bundle of some number of small pictures.
(2) No estimate; show di harvest exactly with big and small pictures.
(3) Pictures wey you draw for one field no suppose pass 8.
y-m-09-08.thinking.0: Find several picture values wey meet di conditions
y-m-09-08.thinking.1: Explain why one picture value no fit work
y-m-09-08.prereq.0: Read di numbers wey big and small pictures represent for picture graph (Grade 3, second semester level)
y-m-09-08.prereq.1: Read how many small pictures dey inside one big picture bundle
y-m-09-08.s.s1.prompt: If one big picture represent 100 kg and one small picture represent 10 kg, you fit show all 4 harvests according to di rules?
y-m-09-08.s.s1.hint.0: Change all 4 harvests to small pictures only (10 kg each) and check whether any one no fit show exactly.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.hint.1: Check which field use di 100 kg big picture, and whether di fields wey no use am fit show with only small pictures.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.o.a: E fit show. For 85 kg and 45 kg, cut one 10 kg picture for half and draw half picture.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.r.a: Di rules get only 2 kinds of pictures, big picture and small picture. Make and use new half picture break di rules.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.o.b: E no fit show. One field no use di 100 kg big picture, so rule (1) no fit stay.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.r.b: Di big picture no need to appear for every field. You fit show value wey smaller than di big picture with small pictures only.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.o.c: E no fit show. 85 kg and 45 kg no fit match exactly with 10 kg pictures.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.r.c: Dis idea check how di small picture value fit with di harvest amounts.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.o.d: E fit show. 30 kg smaller than di big picture, but you fit show am with 3 small pictures.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.r.d: 30 kg correct, but check whether you fit show all di other fields' harvest too.
y-m-09-08.s.s1.explain: With 10 kg per small picture, you no fit show di 5 kg for di ones place of 85 kg and 45 kg. 120 kg and 30 kg fit show, but to show all 4 harvests exactly, di small picture value must divide all 4 numbers evenly.
y-m-09-08.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 combinations of big picture B kg and small picture s kg, with different big picture values, wey follow all rules (1) to (3).
y-m-09-08.s.s2.hint.0: First choose di number wey one small picture go represent. Check whether all 4 harvests fit show as multiples of dat number.
y-m-09-08.s.s2.hint.1: After you choose di small picture value, choose big picture value and count how many pictures each field from 가 to 라 need. Check say e no pass 8.
y-m-09-08.s.s2.ok.c1: B and s na natural numbers and di big picture bigger.
y-m-09-08.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg make s a natural number wey be 1 or more, and B a natural number bigger than s.
y-m-09-08.s.s2.ok.c2: One big picture na bundle of some number of small pictures. (Rule 1)
y-m-09-08.s.s2.fail.c2: Abeg make B multiple of s. (Rule 1)
y-m-09-08.s.s2.ok.c3: You fit show all 4 harvests exactly. (Rule 2)
y-m-09-08.s.s2.fail.c3: One harvest no fit show exactly with small picture s. (Rule 2)
y-m-09-08.s.s2.ok.c4: No field get more than 8 pictures. (Rule 3)
y-m-09-08.s.s2.fail.c4: One field get more than 8 pictures. (Rule 3) Change di big picture and count again.
y-m-09-08.s.s2.explain: Di small picture must show 85, 45, 120, and 30 exactly, so e must be 5 kg (with 1 kg, pictures go too plenty). Big pictures of 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, and 40 kg follow di rules. With 10 kg, field 가 get 12 pictures, and with 50 kg, field 다 get 9 pictures, wey pass 8.
y-m-09-08.s.s3.prompt: Choose 2 picture values wey you just make, compare dem, and write which one make di picture graph easier to read and why.
y-m-09-08.s.s3.hint.0: For each of di 2 picture values, write how many pictures field 가 and field 나 need; put dem side by side and compare.
y-m-09-08.s.s3.hint.1: Also check di difference between di field wey get di most pictures and di field wey get di fewest.
y-m-09-08.s.s3.placeholder: Example: ... kg and ... kg easier because ...
y-m-09-08.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You really count di pictures for all 4 fields using di picture value wey you choose?
y-m-09-08.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Compared with di other picture value, you explain with numbers (number of pictures) which part easier?
y-m-09-08.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You think about say “easy to read” fit different from person to person?

y-m-09-08.s.s3.model.1: 25 kg and 5 kg also work, but field 가 get 4 big pictures and 4 small pictures, 8 altogether, wey fit confuse person. With 30 kg and 5 kg, field 가 get only 4 big pictures, so e easy to read.

y-m-09-09.title: Can we talk about di whole school from wetin we ask for di library?

Seou group wan know “wetin students for our school want do pass during break time.” Seou ask 20 students wey dey borrow books for di library during break time and make table. Our school get about 300 students.

y-m-09-09.thinking.2: Rewrite conclusion to fit di evidence

y-m-09-09.prereq.1: Know wetin “di whole school” and “some” mean
y-m-09-09.s.s1.prompt: Wetin best explain di connection between Seou statement and di table?
y-m-09-09.s.s1.hint.0: Write where di 20 students for di table dey, and imagine whether result fit different if you ask students for di playground di same question.
y-m-09-09.s.s1.hint.1: Compare whether "students for our school" for Seou sentence and "20 students" for table na the same group.
y-m-09-09.s.s1.o.a: Reading na the most with 11 students, so e na the most among all school students too.

y-m-09-09.s.s1.r.c: You need look who dem ask, no be how many students dem ask.

y-m-09-09.s.s1.r.d: Just increasing number of people no solve am. Which kind students those 100 be fit matter more.
y-m-09-09.s.s1.explain: Numbers for table na story about 20 students wey we meet for library. Students wey come library likely to like reading, so you no fit talk say e show wetin whole school think as e be. Even if you add more people, asking at same place still get same problem.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.prompt: To get result wey you fit talk about whole school, how e good to change di survey? Choose all methods wey fit.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.hint.0: For each method, write which students for school you go leave out if you ask dem that way.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.hint.1: Mark methods wey leave nobody out or include plenty different students evenly.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.o.a: Choose few students from each class by drawing lots and ask dem same question
y-m-09-09.s.s2.r.a: Dis thinking make sure say plenty different students from school dey included evenly.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.o.b: Ask only students wey dey play for playground during break.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.r.b: Na only place change, from library to playground; same thing be say you ask only one side of students.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.o.c: Make all students for school write their answer to same question on paper and submit am.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.r.c: Dis thinking put every student for school inside survey group.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.o.d: Ask same question to 20 closest friends.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.r.d: Close friends often get similar thoughts, so e hard for dem to represent whole school.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.o.e: Choose 20 students wey seem like dem go answer well and ask dem.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.r.e: If person wey dey do survey choose students, thinking fit lean one side.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.explain: Choosing evenly from each class and asking dem, or asking all students for school, include plenty students without leaving any out. Asking only students at one place, close friends, or students wey survey person choose fit lean one side.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.acc.0: Choosing evenly and asking na good too. But you gatz decide how many to choose from each class and how. Better still, also choose method of asking all students for school.
y-m-09-09.s.s2.acc.1: Asking all students for school na good too. E take long and some students fit no submit paper. Better still, also choose method of choosing evenly and asking.
y-m-09-09.s.s3.prompt: Rewrite Seou last statement so e fit range wey table show. Write am so who dem ask and numbers for table clear.

y-m-09-13.prereq.0: Read di number of students for each item from table and find di biggest item (Grade 3 level)

y-m-09-13.topic: Check whether sentence wey explain a table match di table, then rewrite am
y-m-09-13.goal: Separate sentences wey di table numbers support from those wey exaggerate. Rewrite di exaggerated sentence to fit di facts so readers no go get wrong idea.
y-m-09-13.material: 30 Grade 3 students each choose one favorite lunch. Di result na pizza 9 students, chicken 8, bibimbap 7, and noodles 6. One student write first draft of article for di school newspaper. Even Grade 1 younger students read dis paper.
y-m-09-13.thinking.0: Check whether one sentence go beyond di evidence
y-m-09-13.thinking.2: Rewrite am to fit di reader

y-m-09-13.s.s1.hint.1: Put di number of students wey choose pizza and di number wey no choose am side by side and compare.

y-m-09-13.s.s1.line.1: Di most students choose pizza, na 9.

y-m-09-13.s.s1.explain: Line 3 go beyond di table. 9 out of 30 students choose pizza, so di other 21 choose other food. “Di most” and “most of dem” no mean di same ting. Lines 1, 2, and 4 match di table.
y-m-09-13.s.s2.prompt: To write “most students choose pizza,” at least how many students suppose choose am?

y-m-09-13.s.s2.o.d: E must be 16 or more. E must pass half of 30.
y-m-09-13.s.s2.r.d: Dis use half as di standard and check whether di number pass am.
y-m-09-13.s.s2.explain: People usually use “most” when di number clear pass half. For 30 students, e must be 16 or more to pass half. Person fit also use stricter rule of 21 or more. Either way, 9 no reach.
y-m-09-13.s.s2.acc.0: E okay to read “most” more strictly. Di point say e must be well above half still be di same.

y-m-09-11.title: We fit know who win while dem still dey count votes?

y-m-09-11.goal: Learn say if dem count only part of data, dem no fit settle result yet; thinking about whether remaining data fit change ranking help find point wey dem fit settle am.
y-m-09-11.material: For class meeting, we vote to choose class representative animal. Three candidates dey: rabbit, turtle, and sparrow, and 30 students vote altogether. y-m-09-11.thinking.1: Correcting your judgment when new data come

y-m-09-11.s.s1.prompt: Counting result dey announce each stage. Each time, choose your thinking.

y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.0.info: 10 votes don open. Rabbit get 5 votes, turtle 3, sparrow 2. 20 votes still never open.

y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Dem never decide am. 20 votes still remain unopened.
y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Dis thinking consider whether remaining votes fit change result.

y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.1.ask: Choose all statements wey describe situation now correctly.
y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.1.after: If turtle or sparrow get plenty of remaining 10 votes, result fit change. We no fit settle am yet, but e okay to talk say rabbit dey advantage.
y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.1.o.a: Rabbit don decide as representative animal, because e dey ahead by 2 votes.

y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.1.r.c: Dis thinking look together at being ahead now and whether remaining votes fit change am.
y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.1.o.d: Sparrow no fit win. E get di fewest.

y-m-09-11.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Dis thinking check whether ranking change even if you assume remaining votes go in worst way.
